lines.caption: This is a tour of the pull request for issues 19 and 24, which make Thunar's tab bar do more.
Files dropped on a tab's label land in that tab's folder, and a double-click on a tab opens its parent folder.
It has three parts: what the PR adds, how it was built and checked, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
First, you drag files over a tab's label, from any view or app.
The label checks the drag carries files, highlights itself, and switches to the tab after half a second.
On the drop it copies, moves or links them, and a middle-button drop asks which.
The files land in the folder that tab shows.
Second, you double-click a tab, or the empty part of the tab bar.
The tab bar checks the setting is on, no modifier is held, and the click wasn't on the close button.
Then the existing Open Parent action runs on that pane's tab. At the root folder nothing happens.
Two new Preferences checkboxes turn the double-click off and always show the tab bar.
Nemo already drops on tabs, and full list views leave no blank space to double-click, so the tab bar is the natural place.
The label only takes file drags. Dragging a tab itself is a different kind of drag, so it works as before.
Each tab's label box becomes a drop target, with a timer that switches tabs, since the label now gets the drag first.
The drop uses the same calls as the path bar's buttons.
The folder and label are held while the ask menu is open, so closing the tab meanwhile can't crash Thunar.
The double-click handler only acts on presses that land on the tab bar itself, and finds the tab under the pointer.
The window now listens for the always-show-tabs setting, so tab bars appear and hide at once.
In short: drop on a tab to move files there, double-click a tab to go up.
Tab dragging, the close button, and the other clicks are unchanged.
The code is in the window and the preferences, plus the test script and this page.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows the path bar's drop code, the owner's notes on issue 19, and the existing tab click handling.
The package was built in this session, with no warnings in the changed files.
The test dragged a file onto another tab's label, and checked it moved there unchanged.
It double-clicked tabs, in one pane and in split view, and checked only that tab went up.
It ticked and unticked the new checkboxes, and saw each take effect at once.
An independent auditor confirmed all fifteen screenshots show what they claim.
Copy, link, the ask menu, the close button and tab dragging were not scripted.
A fresh review agent read the diff before the first push and found two medium and three low issues.
The fixes skip tabs scrolled out of view, make the test unable to pass by accident, and drop late file lists.
Two small lows were kept, since they match the code around them.
CI's review then found ten lows. Five are fixed, and the owner accepted four that follow the issues.
After the merge, the owner drags tabs between panes by hand and runs the split-view crash check.
Part 3. What comes later. Nothing depends on these issues.
So what's left is trying the drops and double-clicks in a real session.
That's it: the tab bar now takes dropped files and goes up a folder on a double-click.
